neighbours.label: the quantity just before the divisor of a rate (the 'meters' in meters per second, the '1' in 1/x): anticipating 'per' or '/'
fire: The jet stream can blow at nearly 300 kilometers per hour over the ocean.
Sound moves through dry air at about 343 meters per second at room temperature.
The old engine turned at a steady 900 revolutions per minute.
Acceleration is measured in units of distance per second squared.
The pump delivers twelve liters per minute to the tank.
Using the power rule, the derivative of ln(5x) equals 1/x again.
The glacier advances roughly two centimeters per day in winter.
Her heart rate rose to 160 beats per minute during the race.
quiet: The jet stream can stretch for nearly 300 kilometers over the ocean.
Sound travelled across the dry valley and echoed for several seconds.
The old engine had covered 900 kilometers before it failed.
The runner stood still for a second and then sprinted away.
The pump holds twelve liters of water in its tank.
Using the power rule, students solved five problems on the board.
The glacier is roughly two kilometers wide at its mouth.
Her heart pounded for a minute after the race.

predictions: Fires on the unit or number right before 'per', 'every' or '/' in a rate; quiet on the same unit words used as plain amounts.
notes: Probes: 'length per unit time' 0.91 (peak ' of'), '150 meters per second' 0.58, 'one revolution every ten days' 0.64, '1/x' 0.71; same units as plain amounts: 'ten meters long' 0.006, 'for one second' 0.012. 'P = W/t' only 0.20. Output promotes 'speed', 'pace'.
